A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REFINED-BIAS research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including the new Appendix A.11 in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original human cue-recognition studies, benchmark comparisons and evaluations across model architectures and training strategies, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an analysis relating CNN receptive-field sizes to cue sensitivity and preference.

M1.justification: The cue-generation pipeline, full-label evaluation, sensitivity metrics and preference equations remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.1. The receptive-field analysis does not modify any model or proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The datasets, ImageNet-1k recognition setting, cue-identification tasks and human-study populations are retained. Appendix A.11 analyzes existing CNN results without adding data or a distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: The cue-conflict, Tartaglini et al. and Burgert et al. comparisons in Table A are unchanged, as are the architecture and training-strategy memberships in Tables B–D. Newly cited receptive-field studies are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Training configurations, preprocessing, human-study procedures, label spaces and cue-evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix A.11 statistically reanalyzes existing CNN scores without changing their benchmark-evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.11 and Figure J investigate whether receptive-field size helps explain the architecture-dependent shape–texture trade-off. This is a focused supplementary correlation analysis using existing models, rather than a controlled architectural ablation.

E5.justification: Figure J introduces Spearman rank-correlation analysis with significance reporting for receptive-field relationships. Existing Pearson/Kendall analyses, t-tests and confidence intervals remain unchanged; no increase in runs or new seed information is reported.

E6.justification: Figure J newly reports receptive-field correlations of 0.938 with Shape-Sens and -0.912 with Texture-Sens, both with p<0.05, alongside a cue-conflict preference correlation. Original accuracy, sensitivity, bias and confidence-interval entries are retained.

T1.justification: The shape/texture definitions, sensitivity and preference equations, and cue-conflict bias formulas are unchanged. The new receptive-field explanation is an empirical hypothesis, with no added mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about reliable cue construction, full-label sensitivity evaluation and clearer model comparisons. Architecture-dependent trade-offs were already claimed in v1; v3 adds supporting interpretation.

C2.justification: Appendix A.11 newly proposes receptive-field size as a partial explanation for the trade-off: larger fields support broader structural information, while smaller fields favor local texture. It explicitly qualifies the correlations as noncausal evidence. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table B newly documents receptive-field sizes for the 14 existing CNNs, and Figure J identifies their literature source. These are additional architectural details, not changed architectures. Training configurations and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds five references, numbered 52–56, concerning receptive-field computation, large kernels and related architectures to support Appendix A.11. The central positioning against cue-conflict and alternative bias benchmarks is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes an accidentally duplicated discussion paragraph, adds Appendix A.11, introduces subsection B.1 and adjusts appendix headings. The existing main narrative is otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure J, encoding receptive-field size through marker area, and expands and relocates Table B with an RF column. Later example figures are retained and renumbered. Table B also acquires an inaccurate 'training strategies' caption and a duplicated explanatory sentence.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.11 adds quantitative support for a plausible explanation of the previously reported architecture trade-off, with an explicit causality caveat and disclosed receptive-field values. Removing the duplicated discussion improves readability. These limited gains outweigh the new Table B caption defects; the central method and empirical validation remain unchanged.
